header.title: How to Repair a Broken, Old Refrigerator
header.description: This guide details how to repurpose a broken, old refrigerator into a custom, insulated enclosure, potentially for a project like a cold storage unit or DIY incubator. It involves removing existing components, building a supporting platform, and reassembling key mechanical parts.

steps.description: This step involves removing the fridge doors and internal components for access and salvage of parts.
actions: Remove the doors
Set aside shelves or drawers
Find the wire leading to the door light
Separate the door light wire from the unit
Remove mechanical parts including wires, fans, compressor, evaporator, and dehumidifiers
steps.part: Doors, shelves, drawers, door light wire, wires, fans, compressor, evaporator, dehumidifiers

steps.description: Cut away the freezer compartment from the DIY fridge unit using a circular saw.
actions: Draw a line around the outside of the unit, just above the freezer storage compartment.
Saw through the line to cut away the freezer compartment.
Ensure you cut through all layers to completely separate it from the bottom half.

steps.description: Construct a platform from 2x4 studs to elevate the refrigerator and provide storage space.
actions: Remove the freezer compartment
Create a platform with 2x4 studs
Secure the unit to the platform
Raise the platform at least 12 inches off the floor
Place two sheets of foam insulation on the platform

steps.description: Apply foam insulation to the fridge compartment, including the top and door, and route the door light wire through it.
actions: Glue sheets of foam insulation on each side of the fridge compartment
Apply insulation to the top of the fridge compartment
Apply insulation to the door of the fridge compartment
Run the wire for the door light through the insulation
Keep the wire available and ready to connect to power

steps.description: Install the condensing unit in a well-ventilated area, ideally in a basement below the refrigerator and connect wiring through the floor.
actions: Place condensing unit in a well-ventilated area
Position condensing unit away from the refrigerator
Connect wiring through the floor
Mount condensing unit to rafters

steps.description: Install the evaporator and thermostat, drill a hole for the refrigerant tube, connect the tube, mount the thermostat, and seal the hole.
actions: Install evaporator and thermostat inside
Drill from inside, through the insulating foam to the outside with a 1 ½-inch bit
Push refrigerant tube through hole
Attaching refrigerant tube to the evaporator tube as specified by the manufacturer
Mount the thermostat on the evaporator
Plug thermostat into thermostat plug located on evaporator
Use putty to seal the hole

steps.description: Connect the tube from the evaporator to the condensing unit using a clamp.
actions: Connect the tube running from the evaporator
Slip the tube over a receiving port
Screw a clamp over the tube to secure it
Consult the manufacturer specifications if necessary

steps.description: Connect the power supply to the components, following manufacturer's instructions if using a kit.
actions: Connect the power supply to the components
Follow manufacturer directions (if using a kit)
Connect to a DC unit
Recharge the car battery occasionally with a battery charger

steps.description: This step allows the user to optionally improve the aesthetic appearance of the finished refrigerator by applying veneer and finish.
actions: Consider if aesthetics are important.
If aesthetics are not important, enjoy your finished project.
If aesthetics are important and you have woodworking skills, apply a 1/4-inch veneer of oak plywood.
Apply construction strength adhesive.
Stain or varnish the veneer to protect the finish.
Admire your work.
Order groceries online.
